grade.first_issue: In the zero-difference branch, the smallest index \(j\) satisfying \(a_j=3\) need not begin the constant tail, so the assertion \(a_j=\cdots=a_n=3\) and hence \(f(3)=3\) is unjustified.
grade.summary: The submission correctly handles \(n=1\), finds the valid \(n=2\) solution, and establishes the divisibility chain of consecutive differences. However, it does not prove the essential exclusion of all \(n\ge3\): both major branches contain invalid algebra or unsupported decisive assertions.
strengths: Correctly verifies \((-1,1,3)\) and introduces the useful relation \(d_1\mid d_2\mid\cdots\mid d_n\).

errors.description: From \(f(x)-3=(x-3)(x-a_{j-1})Q(x)\), the proof incorrectly inserts an additional factor \(3\); the resulting impossible inequality does not follow.
In the nonzero-difference branch, \(Q(a_{n-2})\) has a sign error, invalidating the subsequent \(n=3\) calculations.
The claim that a divisor check leaves only \(m=-1\) is not demonstrated, and the entire \(n>3\) case is dismissed merely by saying that growth precludes solutions.
The case where the constant tail begins at \(a_1=3\) is not handled.
The \(n=2\) integer-root check omits the possible divisor \(a_1=-1\), although direct substitution rules it out.
